en: Udāna 4.5 Nāgasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Kosambī in Ghosita’s Park.
Now at that time the Blessed One was living crowded with bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, male lay followers, female lay followers, kings, royal ministers, and followers of other sects and their disciples.
Being crowded, he lived in discomfort and lacked ease.
Then it occurred to the Blessed One:
“At present, I dwell crowded with bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, laymen, laywomen, kings, royal ministers, and followers of other sects and their disciples.
Being crowded, I dwell in suffering and lack of ease.”
"What if I were to dwell alone, withdrawn from the group?
Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Kosambī for alms.
Having walked for alms in Kosambī, after his meal, on his return from the alms round, he himself set the lodging in order.
Taking his bowl and robe, without informing his attendant, without taking leave of the community of monks,
he set out alone, without a companion, on a wandering tour toward Pālileyyaka.
Wandering by stages, he eventually arrived at Pālileyyaka.
There the Blessed One was dwelling at Pārileyyaka, in the protected forest grove at the foot of the Bhaddasāla tree.
And a certain great bull elephant was dwelling there, surrounded by elephants, female elephants, elephant calves, and elephant cubs.
He ate grass with its tips broken off, while they ate his broken-off branches, and he drank turbid water.
He drinks the water, and as he emerges from the bathing pool, female elephants pass by, rubbing their bodies against his.
Being thus crowded, he dwells in discomfort and lacks ease.
Then it occurred to that noble elephant:
“Indeed, at present I dwell crowded by male elephants, female elephants, elephant calves, and elephant cubs;
I eat grass with its tips broken off, they eat my broken-off branches, I drink turbid water,
and when I have emerged from the bathing pool, female elephants go along rubbing their bodies against mine.”
“Crowded, I do not dwell in comfort or ease.
What if I were to live alone, withdrawn from the herd?
Then that bull elephant, having departed from the herd, approached Pālileyyaka, the protected forest grove at the foot of the Bhaddasāla tree, where the Blessed One was staying.
Thereupon, that great elephant made the area where the Blessed One was staying free of green grass, and with his trunk, he presented the Blessed One with drinking water and water for washing.
Then, while the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind:

"In the past, I lived crowded among bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, laymen, laywomen, kings, royal ministers, and followers of other sects and their disciples; being thus crowded, I lived in suffering and discomfort."
“I am now living untroubled by monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, kings, royal ministers, members of other sects, and their disciples; being untroubled, I dwell in happiness and comfort.
Then this reflection arose in the mind of that noble elephant:
“In the past, I lived crowded among male elephants, female elephants, elephant calves, and elephant cubs.”
I ate grass with its tips cut off; they ate my broken-off branches;
I drank turbid water; and when I emerged from the bathing place, female elephants came along, rubbing their bodies against mine.
Thus, being beset, I lived in suffering and discomfort.
At present, I dwell untroubled by male elephants, female elephants, elephant calves, and elephant cubs;
I eat grass with its tips intact, and they do not eat my broken-off branches;
I drink undisturbed waters, and when I have emerged from the bathing pools, the female elephants do not rub their bodies against mine.
“They go; being untroubled, I dwell in happiness and comfort.
Then the Blessed One, having understood his own seclusion and having known with his own mind the reflection in the mind of that elephant-nāga, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:
“This is the nāga’s [union] with a nāga...”
Of an elephant with tusks like plow-poles,
the mind is brought into harmony with the mind when the one mind finds delight.
The fifth.
